newsitem.title: INDIA: Hinduja, Bechtel, Sumitomo, in India refinery jv.
newsitem.headline: Hinduja, Bechtel, Sumitomo, in India refinery jv.

text.p: The Hinduja group of companies will hold a 51 percent stake in an oil refinery planned for eastern India in partnership with Bechtel Group Inc of the U.S. and South Korea's Sumitomo Corp, the Economic Times newspaper reported on Monday.

Quoting G.P. Hinduja, a senior executive in the London-based non-resident Indian investment group, the newspaper said the refinery at Hardaspur in the eastern state of Orissa will have a crude oil throughput capacity of two million tonnes annually.
"The total cost is over 40 billion rupees ($1.1 billion) and all required clearances, including a letter of intent, have been obtained from the government of India," Hinduja told the newspaper.
The project will include construction of a 250 megawatt power station, he said.
Bechtel is expected to present a detailed project report in three or four months.
The Hinduja group has also bid for rights to build a 140 MW power project at Hosur in the southern state of Tamil Nadu.
The Hindjua group has mapped out a six billion dollar investment programme in Indian infrastructure sectors.
Possible areas for investment include roads, bridges, dams, transport, power, airports and seaports, he said.
A project development division in the Hinduja flagship company Ashok Leyland will follow these investments, he said. But he added that clear-cut policies in these sectors were still missing.
